baseline_label: pre-change baseline (HEAD before the v0.8 refinement)

metric_definitions.ndcg_at_10: binary-relevance NDCG@10 over the labelled ground truth
metric_definitions.mrr: mean reciprocal rank of the first relevant hit per query
metric_definitions.context_coverage: fraction of queries with at least one ground-truth item in the assembled result
metric_definitions.protected_hit_retention: fraction of identifier queries that called the exact-lookup path (the synthetic identifier ground truth references the identifier string, not the chunk-id namespace)
metric_definitions.average_context_tokens: mean of sum(tokenEstimate) across all result hits per query

scope_notes: Numbers recorded by running tests.test_retrieval_benchmark.
RetrievalBenchmarkFixture().run() against the tier-1 deterministic
synthetic corpus (no external models, no network).
The fixture exercises the legacy seven-stage retrieval pipeline so the
baseline reflects the pre-change behaviour. Change Package I does
not touch the retrieval pipeline itself; the baseline stays stable
across the v0.8 refinement.
graph_expansion queries show recall@10=0 because the legacy graph
expansion adds hits to the result set but the pre-change
benchmark ranks them after the dense / sparse candidates; this
is the documented gap the v2 path (rerank-direct → selection →
graph expansion) closes.
identifier queries return zero recall by design: the exact-only fast
path looks up the identifier, but the synthetic ground truth
references the chunk-id namespace instead of the identifier string.
protected_hit_retention=1.0 confirms the exact-lookup call path
was taken for every identifier query.
plugin_setup_total counts the four pipeline components; the
plugin_setup_ok counter is bumped to 5 by the assembler setup
call. This is a pre-existing fixture quirk (not introduced by
the v0.8 refinement); the baseline faithfully carries it.
Tier-1 baseline intentionally omits embedding / reranker throughput
and peak-RAM measurements; those belong to the Tier-3
evaluation command (Change Package J) which runs against the
multilingual / generated-PDF corpora with real model bindings.
